summary: The Spring Ledger, working construction W (noncanonical; not author-approved). Built on the original 30-Book architecture (PR #551), which it does not modify. It keeps the original identity, the three co-governing engines (Ledger, Source, Old Hand) and the five arcs. Books 1-15 keep the original's events. The working construction corrects one thing in them: Book 1 reads the share-marks as evidence, and the first partial reading of the script is Book 8. It also states two things the original left implicit: the Hollow Gate, and the status of the stewardship tally. Arc IV (Books 19-22) is constructed as two conflicts. The Counted Rota: a lineage's channel repair gives it a Special Draw Right, and hand-light share-holders have draw converted in proportion to the hands they cannot return. Two Practices, One Gate: the counted Turn and the gift practice contest the Hollow Gate, and a rotating Gate Table sets its schedule with no authority over the record. Book 23 inherits genuine but seasonal abundance, drawn unevenly by the best-handed houses, and a belief that abundance needs no work. Book 30 is the Long Return, a deep-store pulse that needs channel labour and a gate routing, which are the two exports of Arc IV. Three finale mechanisms are held open for author choice: A (noncoercive mutual dependence), B (allotted binding rota under a bounded authority) and C (ratified trigger, the agent-proposed working direction for testing and not chosen). Whether shared accounting binds, the flood, the Compact's fate and the stance toward reform are not decided here. Also not decided: whether the Hollow Gate and the Gate Table are accepted parts of the world, and which body ratifies the instrument that Alternative C depends on.

nodes.title: Central question
nodes.summary: Who gives back the water, and must giving be counted? The question changes meaning as the Old Hand readings change what a return is, and it is answered differently by each finale mechanism.

nodes.title: Hands and draw
nodes.summary: Who gives return labour, and who is counted for draw. This is the series' governing variable. Until Book 19 draw follows shares alone. From Book 20 it partly follows hands owed. Each finale mechanism answers the question differently.

nodes.title: Custody of the record
nodes.summary: Who holds the Ledger and on whose authority. Custody is the Stone Hall's source of legitimacy until Book 5. Public access to the credit record begins in Book 5. Custody of the master record is contested until Book 15 and plural after the Reading Hall is founded.

nodes.title: Keeping the channels
nodes.summary: Who performs the return labour that keeps the spring balanced, and at what cost to families with few hands. Old lineages hold the repair skill from Books 9-11. From Book 20 lineage crews carry channel repair under a Special Draw Right, and households that can meet the rota carry the rest.

nodes.title: Reading the First Stones
nodes.summary: Who may read the oldest script and which reading becomes binding. Book 1 reads the share-marks as evidence, not the script. Partial readings of the script are Books 8 and 12, and the full reading is Book 15.

nodes.title: Ledger engine
nodes.summary: Recorded shares set the draw. Credit can be falsified or favoured (Book 1), opened to public access (Book 5), traded (Book 6), re-read as gift or contract (Book 15), and from Book 20 partly set by hands owed. Each change alters who must return labour.

nodes.title: Source engine (physical commons)
nodes.summary: The spring's balance follows the gap between draw and return. Thinning leaves channels dry and floods wild water below; surfeit brings stagnant pools and fever. It responds to balance rather than to any character's intention. Its deep-store pulse, the Long Return, is predicted from Book 23 and arrives in Book 30.

nodes.title: Old Hand engine (interpretive legitimacy)
nodes.summary: Readings of the First Stones change what a share is: debt (Stone Hall), gift (Terrace Council) or contract (Mill Compact). A reading changes whether returns are recorded and therefore the balance on the Source.

nodes.title: The seasonal turn
nodes.summary: The rhythm of return labour across the terraces, repeated each season with changing participants. It makes belonging visible and provides the recurring scene texture across Books.

nodes.title: The counted Turn (high terraces)
nodes.summary: Labour matched to shares in the high terraces, run by the Council since the Turn in Book 6: each share returns labour by rota, and draw still follows shares. The counted Turn's labour holds the high cistern against surfeit. The stewardship tally, from Book 15, records that labour as a record of care for this practice; it does not hold the water.

nodes.title: The gift practice (Lower Ammen)
nodes.summary: Labour given without a count, from the one-season Unmeasured Return in Book 15 onward. It keeps the lower channels working by release at need, and it depends on the Gate for that release.

nodes.title: The Hollow Gate
nodes.summary: The sluice that divides the high cistern's release between the upper and lower channels. The Council has set its schedule since the Turn. In the Book 15 trial the high cistern showed surfeit. The Source responds to the balance between draw and return, and surfeit is too much return, or stored water with no draw. The construction assumes that the trial's uncounted return exceeded the draw the Turn counted, so the surplus showed in the high cistern. The original does not name this mechanism, and the author may reject it. Release draws the cistern down and cannot raise it. The schedule is the object of the Book 21 conflict.

nodes.title: The Lowfen channel
nodes.summary: The lower channel that carries Lower Ammen's wells. It breaks in the thaw of Book 19 and is rebuilt by lineage crews in Book 20. Its lowest terrace is where a declined share runs wild.

nodes.title: A declined share
nodes.summary: A household's exit from the rota in Book 21. It forfeits its share, so its water goes wild and runs down the lowest Lowfen terrace. This is a physical cost of declining, not the act of a villain.

nodes.title: The Long Return (pulse)
nodes.summary: A deep-store pulse in Book 30, predicted by the Balance Stones cut in Book 23. It needs channel labour before its date and a Gate schedule that routes it. The routing decides which channel takes the surge, and that choice belongs to the valley.

nodes.title: Wonder at a responsive order
nodes.summary: The reader's sense that the valley's order is larger and more responsive than any institution assumed.

nodes.title: Everyday belonging
nodes.summary: The warmth of shared labour and meals, which the series must keep specific across generations.

nodes.title: Consequential loss
nodes.summary: Grief and anger that follow from changed standing: those once credited lose standing, and those once uncounted gain it. From Book 20, those whose draw is cut for hands they cannot return also lose standing.

nodes.title: Hopeful flourishing
nodes.summary: The earned sense that a shared practice can outlast the institution that began it. The finale must show the cost.

nodes.title: Stone Hall (Reckoners)
nodes.summary: Hereditary keepers of the Ledger. Under this working path the Hall splits in Book 5, as the original has it, and a remnant under Keeper Corrow continues as a dissenting institution. Typed as other because v2 has no institution category.

nodes.title: Terrace Council
nodes.summary: Formed in Book 6 from families who take the Turn. Runs the counted Turn in the high terraces, keeps the stewardship tally from Book 15, and sets the Hollow Gate schedule until the Gate Table takes it in Book 22. Holds the gift reading as legitimate.

nodes.title: Mill Compact
nodes.summary: Lowland grain-buyers who purchase shares once records open. Their purchased draw carries no return labour. They pursue contract-debt and trade interests from outside the valley and have their own Book 27-29 bid.

nodes.title: Reading Hall
nodes.summary: Founded after the full reading in Book 15 to make the First Stones publicly readable. Keeps the public record and its readings. Publishes the Gate gauge reading (Book 22) and the Balance Stones (Book 23). It has no authority over the schedule.

nodes.title: Maintenance lineages
nodes.summary: Old maintenance lineages (Ysa Trant's) who carry channel-maintenance skill from Books 9-11. From Book 20 they hold a Special Draw Right, conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage. Working design: revocable by the Council. Whether it stays revocable is open question 5.

nodes.title: Gate Table
nodes.summary: A rotating inter-community body formed in Book 22 to set the Hollow Gate schedule from the gauge reading. Seats for each practice, and one seat drawn by lot from households without lineage craft. It holds power over the schedule only, with no authority over the record, the shares or any practice.

nodes.title: Epic fantasy
nodes.summary: Governing genre: the quest is to understand a physical commons that answers choices, not to defeat a rival power.

nodes.title: Pastoral belonging
nodes.summary: Supporting genre: belonging produced by shared return labour and eroded by unshared draw.

nodes.title: Political-institutional
nodes.summary: Supporting genre: institutions compete for legitimacy over custody and distribution of the record and of the Gate schedule. Governs Arc 2 at phase level.

nodes.title: Mystery and discovery
nodes.summary: Tertiary genre: partial knowledge of the record and the spring changes choices; readings are staged so discovery advances by Book.

nodes.title: Finale Alternative A (not chosen)
nodes.summary: Noncoercive coordination by mutual dependence: gate dependence, pair-hands, a care floor, and a Gate Table with no record authority. Draw is decoupled from hands; care is counted and nothing is owed. Failure modes: correlated shock, lowland draw left unhanded, and surveillance of the tally.

nodes.title: Finale Alternative B (not chosen)
nodes.summary: An allotted binding rota for the rebuild window, with lot-drawn one-cycle Table seats, a sunset, a care floor, and grain-labour from the Compact. Hands are owed in proportion to draw, and inside the window a shortfall is a deficit to repay, not a cut in water. Failure modes: standing power through schedule, and the Hall's custody returning under another name.

nodes.title: Finale Alternative C (not chosen; working direction for testing)
nodes.summary: Ratified in Books 27-29: normal seasons follow Alternative A, and a published Balance Stones threshold activates Alternative B's rota for a fixed window. The valley chooses the rule before the threshold is crossed. Failure modes: the threshold becomes an authority, activation by the Reading Hall's reading may be unchecked, ratification fails in calm years, and the gauge is disputed.

phases.title: Reckoned Water

trope_functions: the field that does not match the record
genre_activations.structural_function: a lower-terrace household finds falsified credit in the share-marks (Book 1), and the public record breaks the Hall's monopoly (Book 5).

phases.reader_experience: wonder at the first hidden chamber under the spring; anger at falsified credit
phases.narrative_function: The Ledger governs. Stone Hall credit is proven false from the share-marks, and a lower terrace runs wild; the Hall's monopoly breaks at a local cost. Book 1 reads the measure-marks as evidence and does not read the script. The first partial reading of the script is Book 8. Protagonist's agency comes from evidence and a coalition, not inheritance.
phases.transition: Records open to public access, so shares become tradable and the spring shows its first recorded thinning.

phases.title: The Turn

trope_functions: the compromise that feeds a new market
genre_activations.structural_function: Mill Compact purchases shares from freed households; draw separates from return and the high cistern thins (Book 6). The Turn is sworn and the Terrace Council forms, and the Council operates the Hollow Gate (Books 7-11).

phases.reader_experience: belonging tested by sale; anger at a market in shares
phases.narrative_function: The Source governs. Open records make shares a commodity. Compact purchases draw water without return labour, so the physical balance is the constraint on what the institutions can do. Maintenance knowledge concentrates in old lineages (Books 9-11). The first partial reading of the script (Book 8) makes the Old Hand contested knowledge.
phases.transition: Maintenance becomes an institution (the Turn), the Hollow Gate has a keeper, and the Old Hand becomes disputed knowledge.

phases.title: The Old Hand

trope_functions: the reading that reframes an earlier debt
genre_activations.structural_function: the complete reading of the First Stones (Book 15) makes the first compact a gift-return; the Stone Hall remnant holds it as debt, the Council as gift, and the Compact as contract. An Unmeasured Return is tried in Lower Ammen and causes surfeit in the high terraces, which forces the stewardship tally to count care, not debt.

phases.reader_experience: wonder that the first compact was not a debt; fear of the surfeit
phases.narrative_function: The Old Hand governs. Legitimacy no longer rests on the Ledger alone. The Unmeasured Return is a costly, physically consequential choice: it stabilises the lower valley and disturbs the high cistern. The stewardship tally records care, not debt, and the counted Turn's labour keeps the high terraces from surfeit. The Reading Hall is founded as a public institution with its own readings.
phases.transition: Legitimacy is contested among three readings. The counted Turn and the gift practice now both run on the same Hollow Gate, and no single institution holds the record.

phases.title: Settled Water

genre_activations.structural_function: Conflict A (Books 19-21): the Lowfen breaks and the few-hands share-holders cannot cover it. Lineage crews repair it for a Special Draw Right, draw is converted in proportion to unreturned hands, and one household declines and its share runs wild. Conflict B (Books 21-22): the counted Turn and the gift practice contest the Hollow Gate, and a rotating Gate Table is formed.

phases.reader_experience: warmth of shared repair; the cost of counting
phases.narrative_function: Co-governance. Ledger, Source and Old Hand share the field, and no single engine dominates. Both conflicts come from settled practice, not from a new antagonist. Conflict A is unequal capacity to maintain shared channels. It makes hands set part of draw for the first time in the series, and it gives lineage crews a claim on draw. Conflict B is two proven practices, the counted Turn and the gift practice, which contest one outlet. The valley answers with a Gate Table that sets the schedule and holds no record.
phases.transition: Water is partly earned by hands. The Gate Table, the Special Draw Right and an ambiguous tally pass to the next generation.

phases.title: Unmeasured

trope_functions: the hidden order answers the people who keep it
genre_activations.structural_function: Book 23: the Brightwater generation inherits genuine but seasonal abundance, drawn unevenly by the best-handed houses, and a belief that abundance needs no work. Book 30: the Long Return's pulse needs channel labour and a routing through the Gate. The valley chooses among Alternatives A, B and C for who gives labour and who is counted for it.

phases.reader_experience: hope that is earned by cost; wonder at the deepest chamber
phases.narrative_function: The Source is the physical deadline. The Long Return is a deep-store pulse, predicted by the Balance Stones from Book 23. It needs two things Arc IV left the valley: channel labour, which is hands, and a Gate schedule that routes the surge. Books 23-26 carry the Brightwater generation's inheritance. Books 27-29 carry the Compact's bid and, under Alternative C, the ratification window. Book 30 chooses among three mechanisms. A is noncoercive mutual dependence, in which care is counted and nothing is owed. B is an allotted binding rota under a lot-drawn, time-limited Table, with grain-labour from the Compact. C is a ratified trigger that activates B's rule only when a published threshold is crossed. The original's three options map onto these: the single measured Turn is B without its guards, and the Compact's settlement is a clause of B or C. The original's adopted outcome is closest to A; its share-plot settlement is an open choice. No option restores the Stone Hall's sole custody.
phases.transition: The series closes locally. A shared practice and the long-range questions continue.

open_questions: Does the spring respond to intent, or only to measured balance? Book 15 gives a partial answer; the full ontology is deliberately not promised.
What do the lowland towns owe Ammen, and what does Ammen owe them?
Which finale mechanism, A, B, C or a third, does the author choose for who gives return labour and who is counted for it? Not decided.
Does the shared accounting of care bind, and in what form? Not decided.
Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent, and what training condition does it carry?
Is the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion a lasting settlement, or a stage the finale must revisit?
Does the Compact accept grain-labour in exchange for settling its claim, and does the Gate Table's schedule reach its lowland draw? Not decided.
Which channel takes the Long Return's surge, and does any household flood? This is an author choice and is not decided.
Does a Balance Stones threshold exist (Alternative C), and who reads it?
Is Hesper's generational motive independent of the author's preference for the Turn's sustainability? Not yet tested.
Do the Old Hand's readings need intermediate states between Books 8 and 15? Not decided.
Who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end?
How many Brightwater shares may be drawn before the Balance Stones restrain them?
Is the Book 30 flood survived without losses or with lasting ones? This is an author choice.
Does reform from within remain the series' stance, and does the Gate Table model it or warn against it? Not decided.
Will any terrace keep a measured ledger in Book 30, and is plurality of practice the intended end state? Not decided.
